title: If you made a great game almost entirely with AI, would you use that as a marketing hook or avoid mentioning it?
author: uskyeeeee
selftext:
Imagine that, at some point in the future, you make a genuinely high-quality game with AI doing the vast majority of the work. Assume the game is good enough to stand on its own, and you’re the first person to achieve that level of quality this way.  
Would you emphasize that it was mostly made by AI, or avoid talking about AI and just promote the game?  
The AI angle could bring enormous attention. Being the first would make it a story people want to share. But much of that attention might turn into arguments about AI rather than interest in playing the game. You could get a huge number of views, very few wishlists, and backlash that follows the game into launch.  
Alternatively, you could leave AI out of your promotional posts and interviews and focus entirely on gameplay. You’d lose a potentially powerful publicity hook, but give the game a chance to be judged on its own.  
Assuming any required platform disclosures are handled, which marketing approach would you choose if your main goal were Steam wishlists and sales?  
Would you try normal marketing first, then bring up AI only if you struggled to get attention? Or would you use the AI story from day one while being “the first” still mattered?  
Have you seen similar situations—even unrelated to AI—where a controversial story helped or hurt a game commercially?

comments.author: KnownPride
comments.body:
The whole idea is already hilarious 

A game exist for fun and to be played.
All other promotion ouside this factor tell me that you're not confident at the game as a game at all

comments.author: -Star-Walker-
comments.body: If you don’t have to label it as „Made with AI“, don’t do it. I‘ve seen it with vegan products in Germany. A cereals company started to label all their vegan products as „Vegan“. They didn’t change anything, they just labeled some of their cereals … and their sales went down.

replies.author: Officialpolygrafix
replies.body:
thats interesting because vegans typically look for a vegan label.   
So in the case where you live, you must have more volume of people that are against veganism and would not buy to spite the vegans, more than you have actual vegans.

replies.author: -Star-Walker-
replies.body:
That’s another discussion. But in short:  
I’m a vegan, I know „my“ products. Almost every vegan knows their products, so they don’t need any label. There’s no win in gaining more vegans here. The funny thing is, there isn’t any reason to be against vegan products.

For declaring a game as „made with/by AI“ there is a real reason, not to support products made with/by AI: Massive copyright infringement.  
Big models are known to be trained on copyrighted material. Almost all published code on GitHub is licensed at least in some way, that you have to mention the original author. Guess how many models are „aware“ of their training data and the bound license agreement.

comments.author: ContactIcy3963
comments.body: A good game made with AI would only be noticed as being made with AI by the disclosure. If that makes sense.

comments.author: RUSuper
comments.body: After starting my project as a hobby I said everywhere that I use AI for making it. I wanted to inspire as many people as I could that had 0 coding experience that they can make something cool and amazing even if they don't know how to code, but I have to admit outside of "pro-ai" circles it is doing poorly as marketing trick. If you really want to market your game I think that part should not be talked about. But if you are fine with AI hate and all you want to do is get Pro-AI crowd and inspire people then it is great saying "made with AI".

replies.author: uskyeeeee
replies.body: I recently made a high-quality game demo entirely with AI, and nobody could tell it was AI-made. I then posted a video using the fact that it was 100% AI-made as the hook, and it got a lot of views and attention. That’s what got me wondering: how much of that attention could actually translate into Steam wishlists?

replies.author: RUSuper
replies.body: I suspect not a lot. I am in the process of ID verification on steam and will know more later on. But apparently there are negative reviews on Steam like "I enjoyed playing it but then I saw it is AI made and giving it negative review" or something like that. I personally didn't look at those things so can't confirm it, but people are saying AI witch hunt is in full force on Steam.

comments.author: Extension_Street_446
comments.body: All the games right now have used AI.

comments.author: Officialpolygrafix
comments.body:
i think there are a number of people that are so Anti-Ai, that it would be a disservice for you to announce it unnecessarily, as it becomes a target on your back.   
I posted to another group about a game i was making, a very high effort game from a game design i've had for 13 years and have been working several months on, and because i had to disclose that it was coded with ai and that i used suno for the music (im an artist so i did the art myself), i literally had someone stalking me on here, downvoting anything i wrote anywhere, even when it wasn't about my game, general comments on made on non related posts it seems.  
Then i learned the block button and it stopped.   
Some people are really crazy about this, but this is the way it's headed whether they like it or not. Same with horse and buggy when cars were made.

comments.author: -Unpaid_Wizard-
comments.body: In a few years time it wont matter.

comments.author: syn_krown
comments.body: Here's a good idea. Get AI to assist in building the engine and editor for your game, then make the game with that editor and engine without using AI for assets or dialogue, then you should be sweet

comments.author: Alternative-Bread411
comments.body:
If someone made a genuinely great game practically entirely with ai, it would be an undeniable game changer whether they wanted to market that fact or not.

Do I think we’re close? No. Ai is fantastic, but I’m doubtful it can make a great game without substantial human creative input, artistic taste defining the style and direction, human perspective in story and dialogue, shaping and iterating the experience. Not having ai create it for us.

Ai doing a sizeable amount of the heavy lifting within that human vision? Like your code example. Absolutely, and probably soon! A great game generated from a few prompts with virtually no hands-on creative involvement? I’m sceptical, if ever.

replies.author: Serious_Bite_7613
replies.body: I'm getting pretty close, I think another month and I will consider putting my game on steam. I did nothing but prompt. If it makes $100 in sales then it covers the cost of making it.

comments.author: Ok-Investment4414
comments.body:
Steam wants your honesty if ai was involved and the level. Most devs using ai just not as much and yes their are the purist who treat it like poison.Get out in front saying it's ai made, at some point people may ask if and do cia/fbi raided syncronized ops to find out if you did or didnt.  
  
Gamers are like animal lovers they are militant and one of the few groups that can rally together to get X done. So yeah say it loud and proud **made with ai** .   
  
Pair it with some bs story about your grandma getting u an Atari u always played with her u kinda sucked but she you win some times. It was a dream  of making a game u could play together then you would def win.   
But life came at u fast... after seeing all those 1 shot vids you tried a free model and taken a back. It wasn't 1 shot but you were blown away ... also add some extra human elements like 9-5 grind (working on reports) but once home u battled with the pesky gpt/claude extra 3hrs a day even got help from the spouse/gf/bf/kid/etc who were amazed and said u could get a job doing this.

And avoid the anti dev and creator statements like - don't need to know programming , saved on voice acting and sound in general , saved on art work etc. Those really piss people off.   
The point is people like people and humane shit u gotta glaze the humane elements don't.You would be surpzied all a those things help in disarming the pitch forkers . Don't need to lie like i did above but def embellish.  also grandma > grandpa in that story and kid / spouse / partner > just u.

comments.author: _Raro
comments.body:
Most game devs use ai and don’t disclose.

There are some very obvious sign but most people, even anti ai people, don’t notice as long as you can avoid the slop look.

comments.author: DoctaRoboto
comments.body:
This feels redundant. In the future, all games will use AI in some capacity, so if you make a good game, it will sell because it will be a good game. Also, a good game doesn't necessarily mean commercial success. If I were you, I would sell the game without boombastic ads, and if the game is a massive success...then go and rub the wounds of the Anti-crowd claiming it was 100% AI-generated.

This will happen eventually anyway; right now, 85% of Japanese devs are openly using AI. Chinese probably 100% lol.

comments.author: shlaifu
comments.body:
no. The bar for AI generation is not that a gamedeveloper can spend time with it and create a good game.
 The bar for AI is that the player can give it a prompt and it will generate a world on the fly - and even that is no longer really all that outstanding, it's just that genie3 only said it could do that but then was kind of a disappointment.
but that's the bar.
